key_insight: The paper extends mixing-plane coupling to compressible reacting flows by enforcing a thermodynamically consistent mixed-out state for non-ideal post-combustor gas mixtures.
engineering_relevance: This enables steady whole-engine turbomachinery simulations that can couple compressor, combustor, and turbine without violating mass, momentum, or energy consistency across interfaces.
method: Outer pressure-root search to satisfy the mixed-out state
Inner enthalpy inversion to handle nonlinear thermodynamic closure
Physical state checks plus power-law pressure sampling for robustness at low normal velocity
evidence_signal: Validated on a quasi-1D interface test, a transonic compressor case, and a KJ66 micro-turbojet whole-engine simulation, with maximum relative mass-flow error below 0.11% and good agreement with experiments.
watch_item: The approach adds algorithmic complexity and requires robust thermodynamic property inversion, which may be sensitive near pressure bounds and low-flow interfaces.
paper_title: Generalised Mixing-Plane Method for Compressible Reacting-Mixture Flows in Steady Multiphysics Turbomachinery Simulations
